title: Messaging & call ads
content:
# Messaging & call ads

Create Meta ads that open a WhatsApp, Messenger or Instagram Direct conversation with POST /v1/ads/messaging, or dial a number with POST /v1/ads/call.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

Create an ad that opens a conversation, not a web page, with `POST /v1/ads/messaging`, or one that dials your number with `POST /v1/ads/call`.

Each call builds the whole hierarchy (campaign, ad set, creative, ad) or attaches creatives to an existing ad set.

## Before you start

You need `accountId` and `adAccountId`. The Page has to be paired with the destination before you call.

For WhatsApp, optional top-level `whatsappPhoneNumber` selects a number already paired with the Page. Omit it to use the Page's default pairing.

## Messaging ads

Each call also picks the call to action, `destination_type` and optimization goal Meta requires for that destination.

`destination` selects where the conversation opens:

| `destination` | Opens in | Call to action | Requires |
|---|---|---|---|
| `whatsapp` | WhatsApp | `WHATSAPP_MESSAGE` | The Page paired with a verified WhatsApp Business number |
| `messenger` | The Page's Messenger inbox | `MESSAGE_PAGE` | A Facebook Page |
| `instagram_direct` | The linked Instagram account's Direct inbox | `INSTAGRAM_MESSAGE` | An Instagram professional account linked to the Page |

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();

const { data: created } = await zernio.messagingads.createMessagingAd({
  body: {
    accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d',
    adAccountId: 'act_1234567890',
    destination: 'messenger',
    name: 'Summer promo, Messenger',
    headline: 'Chat with us',
    body: 'Get a personal quote in 2 minutes.',
    imageUrl: 'https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg',
    budgetAmount: 20,
    budgetType: 'daily',
    currency: 'USD',
    countries: ['US', 'ES']
  }
});

const adId = created.ad._id;
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()

created = client.messaging_ads.create_messaging_ad(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    ad_account_id="act_1234567890",
    destination="messenger",
    name="Summer promo, Messenger",
    headline="Chat with us",
    body="Get a personal quote in 2 minutes.",
    image_url="https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg",
    budget_amount=20,
    budget_type="daily",
    currency="USD",
    countries=["US", "ES"],
)

ad_id = created["ad"]["_id"]
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/messaging" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
    "destination": "messenger",
    "name": "Summer promo, Messenger",
    "headline": "Chat with us",
    "body": "Get a personal quote in 2 minutes.",
    "imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg",
    "budgetAmount": 20,
    "budgetType": "daily",
    "currency": "USD",
    "countries": ["US", "ES"]
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`), trimmed. `adType` tells you which shape you got:

- `single` carries one `ad`.
- `multi`, for a request with several creatives, carries `ads`, `platformCampaignId` and `platformAdSetId` instead.

```json
{
  "adType": "single",
  "message": "CTM ad submitted to Meta for review",
  "ad": {
    "_id": "66d4a1b2c3e4f5a6b7c8d9e7",
    "name": "Summer promo, Messenger",
    "status": "pending_review",
    "reviewStatus": "in_review",
    "platformObjective": "OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT",
    "platformAdId": "120260000000000002",
    "platformCampaignId": "120250000000000006",
    "platformAdSetId": "120250000000000007"
  }
}
```

The ad set carries the matching `destination_type` with `CONVERSATIONS` optimization, and the campaign objective defaults to `OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT`. Send `objective` to override it.

Both creative shapes work, with an image or a `video`:

- the single-creative fields above
- `creatives[]` for N ads in one ad set

Unlike `POST /v1/ads/create`, sending both is a `400` rather than ignoring the top-level fields. Either shape also goes on an [existing ad set](#attach-to-an-existing-ad-set).

Targeting takes the full geo shape, not only `countries`. For a local business, pass `cities`, `regions`, `zips`, `metros` or `customLocations`, with keys from [the targeting search](/platforms/meta-ads/targeting#look-up-city-and-region-keys).

The `["US"]` default applies only when no geo field at all is present. A `cities` request targets that city and nothing else.

## Targeting, budget and schedule

Messaging and call ads take the same campaign, ad set and targeting fields as `POST /v1/ads/create` on Meta, built by the same code:

- **Targeting**: every [targeting field](/platforms/meta-ads/targeting): `languages`, `gender`, `excludedLocations`, `behaviors`, `workPositions`, `incomeTier`, `userOs`, `audienceInclude` / `audienceExclude`, `savedTargetingId` and the nested `targeting` object.
- **Raw targeting**: `rawTargeting` is a Meta targeting spec sent as the base layer, for anything the flat fields cannot express. An example is a layered `flexible_spec` (entries AND together, ids inside one entry OR).
  - Flat fields you also send win per key.
  - With `rawTargeting`, the US and `advantage_audience` defaults are not added. Include `targeting_automation` in it or send `advantageAudience`.
- **Campaign budget**: `budgetLevel: "campaign"` puts the budget and bid strategy on the campaign (Advantage campaign budget). The default, `adset`, keeps it on the ad set.
- **Schedule**: `startDate` and `endDate` take an ISO 8601 date or date-time.
  - A value with an offset is used as is. One without (`"2027-01-15T10:00:00"`) is read in the ad account's timezone.
  - A date-only end runs to 23:59:59 local.
  - A `lifetime` budget requires `endDate`.
- **Special ad categories**: `specialAdCategories` and `specialAdCategoryCountry` on the new campaign.

```json
{
  "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
  "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
  "destination": "whatsapp",
  "name": "Quick launch, persona A",
  "headline": "Talk to a specialist",
  "body": "Get a quote on WhatsApp in minutes.",
  "description": "Replies within the hour",
  "imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg",
  "budgetAmount": 50,
  "budgetType": "daily",
  "budgetLevel": "campaign",
  "startDate": "2027-01-15T09:00:00",
  "endDate": "2027-02-15",
  "gender": "female",
  "languages": ["en", "es"],
  "rawTargeting": {
    "geo_locations": { "countries": ["US"] },
    "flexible_spec": [
      { "interests": [{ "id": "6003107902433" }, { "id": "6003139266461" }] },
      { "behaviors": [{ "id": "6002714895372" }] }
    ],
    "targeting_automation": { "advantage_audience": 0 }
  }
}
```

`description` is the link description, separate from `headline` and `body`. It is Meta's `link_data.description`, or `video_data.link_description` on a video.

Meta shows it mainly on Facebook Feed, under the headline, when there is room. Instagram, Stories, Reels and Messenger placements do not display it.

It also goes per entry in `creatives[]`, and cannot be combined with an existing post.

<Callout type="warn">
The Page-to-destination pairing must exist before you call. A missing pairing is Meta subcode `2446886` inside a `platform_error` envelope.
</Callout>

`POST /v1/ads/ctwa` is the deprecated predecessor of `destination: "whatsapp"`. It stays available for existing integrations ([click-to-WhatsApp ads](/platforms/meta-ads/ctwa)).

To attribute conversions that happen inside the WhatsApp thread, see [Conversions API for business messaging](/platforms/whatsapp/ctwa#conversions-api-for-business-messaging).

## Reuse an existing post

Send one of these instead of `headline`, `body` and `imageUrl` / `video`, per creative or at the top level:

- `existingPostId`, Zernio-resolved the same way `postId` resolves on a boost
- a raw Facebook `objectStoryId` (`pageId_postId`)

No media is uploaded and the organic post is kept as-is:

```json
{
  "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
  "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
  "destination": "whatsapp",
  "name": "Reuse existing reel",
  "existingPostId": "811889972008357_123456789"
}
```

`existingPostId` and `objectStoryId` are mutually exclusive with each other. They are also exclusive with `headline`, `body`, `imageUrl`, `video` and `welcomeMessage`.

This only works on messaging and CTWA. Call ads still need a fresh creative.

## Attach to an existing ad set

`adSetId` adds the creatives to a messaging ad set you already have, instead of building a campaign around them.

The ad set keeps its learning phase. That makes this the way to refresh a creative without resetting delivery.

Either creative shape works with it. The target ad set's `destination_type` has to match the ad's `destination`: a WhatsApp ad needs a WhatsApp ad set, or Meta would take an ad that never delivers.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/messaging" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
    "destination": "messenger",
    "adSetId": "120250000000000007",
    "name": "Summer promo, new creative",
    "headline": "Chat with us",
    "body": "Get a personal quote in 2 minutes.",
    "imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/promo-v2.jpg"
  }'
```

Response (`201`), trimmed:

```json
{
  "adType": "single",
  "ad": {
    "_id": "66d4a1b2c3e4f5a6b7c8d9e9",
    "status": "pending_review",
    "reviewStatus": "in_review",
    "platformAdId": "120260000000000004",
    "platformAdSetId": "120250000000000007"
  }
}
```

The ad set already owns the budget, the targeting and the schedule. Alongside `adSetId`, these fields are rejected with a `400` rather than quietly dropped:

- the budget fields and `budgetLevel`
- `startDate` and `endDate`
- `objective`, `campaignStatus` and `existingCampaignId`
- the special ad category fields
- the targeting fields, except `ageMin`, `ageMax`, `placements` and `advantageAudience`

The error reads: "adSetId attaches to an existing ad set, which already owns budgetAmount. Remove it."

Without `adSetId`, the budget fields swap back to required.

## Add an ad set to an existing campaign

`existingCampaignId` creates the new messaging ad set under a campaign you already have, with its own targeting, schedule and creatives. For example, one ad set per persona under one campaign.

The campaign's objective must be `OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT`, `OUTCOME_SALES` or `OUTCOME_LEADS`.

```json
{
  "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
  "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
  "destination": "whatsapp",
  "existingCampaignId": "120250000000000006",
  "adSetName": "Persona B, procurement leads",
  "name": "Quick launch, persona B",
  "headline": "Talk to a specialist",
  "body": "Get a quote on WhatsApp in minutes.",
  "imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg",
  "countries": ["US"],
  "workPositions": [{ "id": "105763692790962" }]
}
```

If the campaign has a campaign budget, it funds the new ad set. Omit `budgetAmount` and `budgetType`: sending them is a `400`, since the campaign would ignore them.

Otherwise they are required and land on the new ad set.

`objective`, `campaignName`, `campaignStatus`, `budgetLevel` and the special ad category fields belong to the campaign. They are rejected with a `400`.

## Different image per placement

`placementAssets` pins a specific image (or video) to each placement group on one messaging ad.

It works the way Ads Manager's "different creative per placement" does: a 4:5 image on Feed and a 9:16 image on Stories and Reels, for example.

It replaces `imageUrl` / `video`. `headline` and `body` stay required as the default copy.

The call to action, `welcomeMessage` and `whatsappPhoneNumber` apply to every placement.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/messaging" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
    "destination": "instagram_direct",
    "name": "Summer promo, Direct",
    "headline": "Chat with us",
    "body": "Get a personal quote in 2 minutes.",
    "placementAssets": {
      "defaultImageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/promo-4x5.jpg",
      "rules": [
        {
          "imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/promo-9x16.jpg",
          "placements": {
            "publisherPlatforms": ["facebook", "instagram"],
            "facebookPositions": ["story", "facebook_reels"],
            "instagramPositions": ["story", "reels"]
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "budgetAmount": 20,
    "budgetType": "daily",
    "currency": "USD",
    "countries": ["US"]
  }'
```

`defaultImageUrl` serves every placement no rule matches. Each rule can also pin its own `headline` or `body`.

A block is all-image or all-video (`defaultVideoUrl` or `defaultVideoId`, plus `rules[].videoUrl` or `rules[].videoId`), never mixed.

The block is the same one `POST /v1/ads/create` takes. See [placement asset customization](/platforms/meta-ads/creatives#placement-asset-customization) for the full shape.

It works with one `destination` and on the [attach shape](#attach-to-an-existing-ad-set). These return a `400`:

- `destinations` (several apps on one ad set): Meta drops the placement rules from a multi-destination creative, and refuses more than one call to action per placement rule (subcode `1885878`). Use one ad set per destination.
- `creatives[]`: send one placement-customized creative per request, and attach more to the same ad set with `adSetId`.
- `imageUrl`, `video`, `existingPostId`, `platformPostId` or `objectStoryId` alongside it.
- `POST /v1/ads/call`.

## Validate without creating

`validateOnly: true` sends the whole ad to Meta as a dry run (`execution_options: validate_only`) and creates nothing. It checks either:

- the campaign, ad set, creative and ad in one check
- the creative and ad against the existing ad set, with `adSetId`

Media is checked by URL, so nothing is uploaded. A success returns `200`:

```json
{
  "validateOnly": true,
  "results": [
    { "node": "campaign", "status": "validated" },
    { "node": "adSet", "status": "validated" },
    { "node": "creative", "status": "validated" },
    { "node": "ad", "status": "validated" }
  ],
  "message": "Validation passed for every node Meta can validate without creating; nothing was created."
}
```

A Meta rejection comes back as the usual `platform_error`.

A dry run supports one creative with `imageUrl`, image `placementAssets`, video `placementAssets` with an id in every slot and no thumbnails, an existing `video.id` or an existing post.

Several creatives, a new `video.url` and video `placementAssets` by URL or with thumbnails need an upload first, so they return `400`.

## Call ads

`POST /v1/ads/call` builds an ad whose call to action is `CALL_NOW`, dialing `phoneNumber` in E.164. `linkUrl` is required alongside it.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: callAd } = await zernio.messagingads.createCallAd({
  body: {
    accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d',
    adAccountId: 'act_1234567890',
    name: 'Book a consult, calls',
    phoneNumber: '+15551234567',
    linkUrl: 'https://example.com/contact',
    headline: 'Talk to an expert',
    body: 'One call, no forms.',
    imageUrl: 'https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg',
    budgetAmount: 30,
    budgetType: 'daily',
    currency: 'USD',
    countries: ['US']
  }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
call_ad = client.messaging_ads.create_call_ad(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    ad_account_id="act_1234567890",
    name="Book a consult, calls",
    phone_number="+15551234567",
    link_url="https://example.com/contact",
    headline="Talk to an expert",
    body="One call, no forms.",
    image_url="https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg",
    budget_amount=30,
    budget_type="daily",
    currency="USD",
    countries=["US"],
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/call" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "adAccountId": "act_1234567890",
    "name": "Book a consult, calls",
    "phoneNumber": "+15551234567",
    "linkUrl": "https://example.com/contact",
    "headline": "Talk to an expert",
    "body": "One call, no forms.",
    "imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg",
    "budgetAmount": 30,
    "budgetType": "daily",
    "currency": "USD",
    "countries": ["US"]
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`), trimmed. Call ads take the same shape as messaging ads, so `adType` is `single` here and `multi` for a request with several creatives.

```json
{
  "adType": "single",
  "message": "Call ad submitted to Meta for review",
  "ad": {
    "_id": "66d4a1b2c3e4f5a6b7c8d9e8",
    "name": "Book a consult, calls",
    "status": "pending_review",
    "reviewStatus": "in_review",
    "platformObjective": "OUTCOME_LEADS",
    "platformAdSetId": "120250000000000008"
  }
}
```

The ad set uses `destination_type: PHONE_CALL` optimizing `QUALITY_CALL`. The campaign objective defaults to `OUTCOME_LEADS`.

<Callout type="warn">
`linkUrl` must be a real website, such as your contact page. Meta rejects a `tel:` URI as the creative's link with subcode `2061006`, because the number rides on the call to action button only.
</Callout>

## Welcome message

`welcomeMessage` replaces the default greeting in the chat that opens. Both fields are required when the object is present:

```json
{
  "welcomeMessage": {
    "text": "How can we help with your quote?",
    "prefillText": "I would like a quote for..."
  }
}
```

`text` is Meta's `page_welcome_message` greeting, shown when the chat opens in place of Meta's generic one.

`prefillText` sits in the user's input box ready to send, in place of Meta's generic opener. One ad can steer the first message toward what it promotes.

On the single-creative shape it is a top-level field. On `creatives[]`, set it per entry. Omit it for Meta's defaults.

## Start a workflow from the ad

`workflowId` binds a [workflow](/products/automations/workflows) in the ad account's profile to the ad. The binding is stored on the ad.

When someone clicks the ad, that workflow starts in the conversation the click opens, ahead of keyword-matched workflows.

It starts on the first message, a postback or a standalone referral carrying the ad id, provided it is active on the receiving account.

A `workflowId` that names no workflow in the profile is a `404`. `POST /v1/ads/call` does not take it.

```json
{
  "destination": "instagram_direct",
  "workflowId": "66d4a1b2c3e4f5a6b7c8d9e1"
}
```

The usual workflow rules still apply:

- no start while another run is live in the conversation
- no start while a human has it
- the workflow's `cooldownHours`

Without a binding, a [`referral` workflow](/products/automations/workflows#triggers-and-nodes) can match the click instead. It reads the ad id from `{{referral.adId}}`.

## Retry safely

A blind retry of `POST /v1/ads/messaging` or `POST /v1/ads/call` creates a second campaign, ad set and ad.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (a UUID per logical ad, up to 255 characters). Reuse it on every retry of the same request:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/messaging" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 3f6c2a1e-8b4d-4f7a-9c1e-2d5b6a7c8e90" \
  -d '{ "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "adAccountId": "act_1234567890", "destination": "messenger", "name": "Summer promo, Messenger", "headline": "Chat with us", "body": "Get a personal quote in 2 minutes.", "imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/promo.jpg", "budgetAmount": 20, "budgetType": "daily", "currency": "USD", "countries": ["US", "ES"] }'
```

The first request with a key creates the ad and stores its response.

A retry with the same key and body replays that exact response with an `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header. It creates nothing.

- The same key with a different body returns `422`.
- A key whose first request is still in flight returns `409`. Back off briefly and retry.

Keys are scoped to your credential and expire after 24 hours. [Idempotency](/guides/idempotency) covers the header across every write endpoint.

## If it fails
A `422` means no Facebook Page resolved for the account:

```json
{
  "error": "No Facebook page found. Connect a Facebook account with a page to create CTM ads.",
  "type": "invalid_request_error",
  "code": "linked_account_required",
  "platform": "meta"
}
```

Connect a Facebook account that manages a Page in the same profile, then retry.

A missing destination pairing fails later, at Meta. It arrives as a `400` with `type: "platform_error"` and subcode `2446886`:

```json
{
  "error": "Meta Ads API error (400; code 100, subcode 2446886): Your Page is not linked to a WhatsApp account.",
  "type": "platform_error",
  "platform": "meta",
  "platformError": { "code": 100, "error_subcode": 2446886 }
}
```

Pair the Page in Meta Business Manager, then retry.

A `403` with `code: "ads_allowance_exceeded"` means the team has no payment method on file and has reached its 500 free live ads. Add a card to resume.

A `502` means Meta accepted the request and then failed to produce the media. Read `platformError.reason`.
